    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Key Observations\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Gender had a strong relationship with survival. The survival rate for females was 74.20%, compared with 18.89% for males.\n",
        "\n",
        "2. Passengers travelling in small family groups generally had higher survival rates. Family sizes of 2, 3, and 4 had survival rates of 55.28%, 57.84%, and 72.41% respectively, while passengers travelling alone had a survival rate of 30.35%.\n",
        "\n",
        "3. The average age of survivors was 28.29 years, compared with 30.03 years for non-survivors. This indicates that the average age difference between the two groups was relatively small."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "_g4uXYOX0WqD"
      }
    },
    {

      "source": [
        "## Conclusion\n",
        "\n",
        "The Titanic dataset EDA shows clear differences in survival across gender and family size.\n",
        "Female passengers had a substantially higher survival rate than male passengers.\n",
        "Passengers travelling in small family groups generally showed better survival rates than those travelling alone.\n",
        "The average ages of survivors and non-survivors were relatively similar."
